name: bge-small-en-v1.5-RIRAG_ObliQA
context_scaling: Inherited unchanged from BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 (config.json max_position_embeddings 512). This derivative does not publish a context-extension recipe of its own.
attention_variant: bidirectional encoder (BERT), full attention, no causal mask
license: not declared (no license tag or LICENSE file on the repo; base BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 is MIT)
notes: ADDED 2026-10-31. A full MultipleNegativesRankingLoss fine-tune of BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 (identical tensor set, 33.36M) on 29,547 regulatory Q&A pairs drawn from the ObliQA corpus, output still 512-d. Wins all six IR metrics in one card table, headline MAP@10 0.6313 vs 0.5462. READ WITH CARE: the 'Fine Tunned' column is the training-time qa_eval score (it appears per-epoch in the training log, 0.6313 at epoch 14.84), so it measures in-domain fit rather than held-out generalisation - the card never says qa_eval is disjoint from the training pairs. No MTEB, no second corpus. Licence NOT DECLARED: no license tag, no LICENSE file, card field reads 'Unknown'; the base is MIT. Repo created 2024-10-26. Confidence 0.4.

benchmarks.name: qa_eval dot_score MAP@10
benchmarks.config: Card '## Evaluation' table '| Metric | Fine Tunned| Base Model |': dot_score_map@10 0.6313 vs base 0.5462 (x100). InformationRetrievalEvaluator on dataset 'qa_eval'; the card never states whether qa_eval is held out from the 29,547 training pairs, so read it as in-domain. Final-epoch training-log value matches the table row (0.6313 at epoch 14.84).

benchmarks.name: qa_eval dot_score precision@10
benchmarks.config: Same table, 0.0984 vs base 0.0842 (x100). Precision is capped by many relevant docs per query, which is why it sits near 10%.
